# Checks reference

<!-- Generated by `aiak rules --format md`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every check is a prompt for human judgement, not a verdict. Severity says how soon a
human answer is needed:

- **high**: resolve, or explicitly accept with a named owner, before relying on the use;
- **warning**: needs a recorded human decision before the next lifecycle stage;
- **info**: worth recording; no action required to proceed.

A citation means the source makes the prompt worth asking. It does not mean the source
requires what the check looks for. Unofficial; not government guidance.

## AIAK-META-001

**Template placeholders remain** (severity: info; skipped when status is: none)

Why: A record that still contains template text reads as complete but is not. Checks on placeholder values say little about the real use.

Sources:

- [ai-assurance-kit design principle: Make uncertainty visible](https://github.com/dsugurtuna/ai-assurance-kit/blob/main/docs/WHY.md)

## AIAK-ACT-001

**Sends or writes without a human approval step** (severity: high; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Actions that send or write change things outside the tool and are hard to undo. Reading and drafting can be checked afterwards; sending and writing need a person, or an explicit decision to go without one, before the action happens.

Sources:

- [ai-assurance-kit design principle: Read freely, write carefully](https://github.com/dsugurtuna/ai-assurance-kit/blob/main/docs/WHY.md)
- [AI Playbook for the UK Government: Principle 4: You have meaningful human control at the right stages](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): GOVERN 3.2](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MAP 3.5](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-ACT-002

**No way to stop the system is recorded** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: A system that acts needs a known, tested way to pause it. Without one, a fault keeps acting while people work out who can switch it off.

Sources:

- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MANAGE 2.4](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [ai-assurance-kit design principle: Read freely, write carefully](https://github.com/dsugurtuna/ai-assurance-kit/blob/main/docs/WHY.md)

## AIAK-ACT-003

**Connector permissions exceed what the system is recorded as doing** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Permissions are what a system can do; the action mode is what the team says it does. A gap between the two is unused power that a fault, a prompt injection or a later change can use.

Sources:

- [ai-assurance-kit design principle: Read freely, write carefully](https://github.com/dsugurtuna/ai-assurance-kit/blob/main/docs/WHY.md)
- [AI Playbook for the UK Government: Principle 3: You know how to use AI securely](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MAP 4.2](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-ACT-004

**Recipients of sends or writes are not recorded** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Who receives an action decides who is affected when it goes wrong. It is also what a later change review compares against.

Sources:

- [ai-assurance-kit design principle: Read freely, write carefully](https://github.com/dsugurtuna/ai-assurance-kit/blob/main/docs/WHY.md)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MAP 1.1](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-DATA-001

**Personal data with no DPIA screening recorded** (severity: high; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Whether a data protection impact assessment is needed is a decision for the organisation, typically involving its data protection lead. The kit cannot make it, but it can notice when no decision is recorded.

Sources:

- [ICO guidance on data protection impact assessments (DPIAs)](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/accountability-and-governance/data-protection-impact-assessments-dpias/)
- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: Development Data Specification (Tier 2)](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)
- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: Risks, Mitigations and Impact Assessments (Tier 2)](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MEASURE 2.10](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-DATA-002

**No retention period recorded for personal data** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: AI tools create new copies of data: prompts, outputs, logs and caches. Each needs a retention period, or it is kept by default.

Sources:

- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: Operational Data Specification (Tier 2)](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MEASURE 2.10](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-DATA-003

**Special category data screened out of a DPIA without a recorded rationale** (severity: info; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Screening special category data as not needing a DPIA may be right, but the reasoning should be findable later.

Sources:

- [ICO guidance on data protection impact assessments (DPIAs)](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/accountability-and-governance/data-protection-impact-assessments-dpias/)

## AIAK-TRANS-001

**ATRS: likely in scope, record the determination** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: The ATRS guidance says the standard is mandatory for all government departments and for arm's-length bodies which deliver public or frontline services or directly interact with the general public; within those organisations it is mandatory for algorithmic tools which "have a significant influence on a decision-making process with public effect, or directly interact with the general public". The kit cannot decide whether a tool is in scope or whether an exemption applies; it only notices the features that make the question worth asking.

Sources:

- [ATRS mandatory scope and exemptions policy](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard-mandatory-scope-and-exemptions-policy)
- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: ATRS purpose and scope](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)

## AIAK-TRANS-002

**Public-facing use with no user notice recorded** (severity: info; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: People who interact with an AI system directly should be able to tell that they are doing so, and where to go if it gets something wrong.

Sources:

- [AI Playbook for the UK Government: Principle 7: You are open and collaborative](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government)
- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: ATRS purpose and scope](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)

## AIAK-ROLE-001

**Builder and assurer appear to be the same person** (severity: high; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: The AQuA Book, which this kit borrows its roles from, keeps the analyst and assurer roles separate: the analyst assures their own work, and formal assurance comes from someone else. (Checked against the final pre-publication draft of its second edition, not the published edition.) The kit treats the builder as the analyst role.

Sources:

- [The AQuA Book: Roles and responsibilities](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-aqua-book)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MEASURE 1.3](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-ROLE-002

**No assurer named** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Proportionate assurance still needs someone to do it. Once a use is approved to build, it should be clear who will check it.

Sources:

- [The AQuA Book: Proportionality](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-aqua-book)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): GOVERN 2.1](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-ROLE-003

**Live with no named maintainer** (severity: high; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: AI systems change after launch: models are updated, data drifts, prompts are edited. A live system with nobody responsible for it degrades without anyone noticing.

Sources:

- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MANAGE 4.1](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): GOVERN 2.1](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: Owner and Responsibility (Tier 2)](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)
- [AI Playbook for the UK Government: Principle 5: You understand how to manage the full AI life cycle](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government)

## AIAK-EVAL-001

**Live with no evaluation evidence** (severity: high; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Going live should rest on evidence that the system works well enough for this use, in conditions like the real ones.

Sources:

- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MEASURE 2.3](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MANAGE 1.1](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [AI Playbook for the UK Government: Principle 5: You understand how to manage the full AI life cycle](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government)

## AIAK-EVAL-002

**Only usage metrics recorded as evidence** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: How often a tool is used says nothing about whether its outputs are right. Usage can rise while quality falls.

Sources:

- [ai-assurance-kit design principle: Usage is not quality](https://github.com/dsugurtuna/ai-assurance-kit/blob/main/docs/WHY.md)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MEASURE 2.3](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-EVAL-003

**Model-graded evidence without a human-checked sample** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: A second model can find problems, but agreement between models is not verification. Model grading needs calibrating against outputs checked by people who know the subject.

Sources:

- [ai-assurance-kit design principle: A second model is a critic, not a verifier](https://github.com/dsugurtuna/ai-assurance-kit/blob/main/docs/WHY.md)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MEASURE 4.2](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MEASURE 1.3](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-EVAL-004

**No independent evaluation recorded** (severity: info; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Evaluation by the team that built a system is necessary but tends to test what the team expected. Someone outside the build team finds different problems.

Sources:

- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MEASURE 1.3](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [The AQuA Book: Roles and responsibilities](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-aqua-book)

## AIAK-REV-001

**Review date has passed** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: A record is a snapshot. After its review date nobody has confirmed that it still describes the system.

Sources:

- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): GOVERN 1.5](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: Updating your ATRS record](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)

## AIAK-REV-002

**No next review date** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Systems in test or live use change. A review date makes someone look again.

Sources:

- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): GOVERN 1.5](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-RISK-001

**Risk above appetite with no owner** (severity: high; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: A risk above the organisation's appetite needs someone accountable for treating it or for accepting it. Without an owner it is recorded but not managed.

Sources:

- [The Orange Book: management of risk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/orange-book)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): GOVERN 1.3](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MAP 1.5](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MANAGE 1.3](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-RISK-002

**Risk above appetite with no control in place** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Planned controls do not reduce risk yet. A risk above appetite should have at least one control in place, or a recorded decision to accept it.

Sources:

- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MANAGE 1.3](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [The Orange Book: management of risk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/orange-book)

## AIAK-RISK-003

**No risks recorded** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: An empty risk list usually means the risks have not been assessed yet, not that there are none. It is a warning, like a missing assurer or review date, so that a record with no risks recorded cannot pass a `--fail-on warning` gate that the same record with an honestly recorded, untreated risk would fail.

Sources:

- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: Risks, Mitigations and Impact Assessments (Tier 2)](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MAP 5.1](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-PURP-001

**No alternatives recorded** (severity: info; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Many problems brought to AI are better solved by fixing the data or the process, or by ordinary automation. Recording what else was considered shows the choice was made.

Sources:

- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: Description and Rationale (Tier 2)](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MANAGE 2.1](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [AI Playbook for the UK Government: Principle 6: You use the right tool for the job](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government)
- [ai-assurance-kit design principle: Fix the data before adding an agent](https://github.com/dsugurtuna/ai-assurance-kit/blob/main/docs/WHY.md)

## AIAK-DEC-001

**Automated decisions with public effect and no challenge route** (severity: high; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: When an output is the decision, the people affected need a way to question it. Rules on solely automated decisions may also apply; that is a question for your data protection lead.

Sources:

- [Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) guidance: Deployment Context (Tier 2)](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-for-organisations-using-the-algorithmic-transparency-recording-standard)
- [ICO guidance on rights related to automated decision-making, including profiling](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/individual-rights/individual-rights/rights-related-to-automated-decision-making-including-profiling/)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MEASURE 3.3](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-DEC-002

**Decision support with no human review described** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Decision support is only support if a person reviews the output with enough time, information and authority to disagree with it.

Sources:

- [AI Playbook for the UK Government: Principle 4: You have meaningful human control at the right stages](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MAP 2.2](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MAP 3.5](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)

## AIAK-LIFE-001

**Status is ahead of the recorded decisions** (severity: warning; skipped when status is: retired)

Why: Approving a build, connecting data, granting access and going live are separate decisions, often for different people. A status with no matching decision suggests one approval is being read as another.

Sources:

- [ai-assurance-kit design principle: Permission to build is not permission to deploy](https://github.com/dsugurtuna/ai-assurance-kit/blob/main/docs/WHY.md)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1): MANAGE 1.1](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [AI Playbook for the UK Government: Principle 10: You use these principles alongside your organisation's policies and have the right assurance in place](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government)
